entries.title: Haggai 1 — Chapter Introduction
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: This - So the prophet triumphs over her. There is none - None like me, or that can contend with me.

entries.title: Haggai 1:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Son - Adoptive son to Shealtiel, being of the royal line, but by nature, son of Pedaiah. Governor - Appointed to this by the Persian king, over the remnant returned out of Babylon. Joshua - A type of the great deliverer; one Joshua leads them into Canaan, another restores the temple.

entries.title: Haggai 1:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Have not enough - But what you eat doth not nourish or satisfy you. Are not filled - Your water quenches not your thirst, your wine does not revive your spirit. None warm - You have no comfort therein. With holes - Loses all his labour.

entries.title: Haggai 1:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Take pleasure - I will accept your offerings, and hear your prayers. Glorified - Shew my majesty and account myself glorified by you also.

entries.title: Haggai 1:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Came to little - But it answered not the expectation. I did blow - I blasted it. Ye run - You with eagerness carry on your own particular buildings.

entries.title: Haggai 1:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Is stayed - God hath forbidden them, to drop down dew.

entries.title: Haggai 1:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Upon men - The very blood, and constitutions of men were changed, and many diseases afflicted them.

entries.title: Haggai 1:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In the Lord's message - ln the words of his master. The people - The whole assembly.

entries.title: Haggai 1:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Lord of hosts - By which name he delights to be known among the returned captives; and it was a name best suited to their present state, compassed on all hands with enemies.
